name: Air-Traffic Control
summary: Every metric is a flight on a calm radar console; the one in conflict moves to HOLD and the human controller clears it.
look: A dark slate-teal ATC console with phosphor range rings, blips with echo trails and mono datablocks, plus buff paper flight strips in teal holders. Conflict is an amber blinking box and a coral strip in the HOLD column.

components.name: Flight progress strip
components.role: paper strip per metric: callsign, value, status

components.name: Strip bay
components.role: ACTIVE and HOLD columns; position tells the story

components.name: Radar PPI
components.role: range rings and blips; the Acme mark is the tower

components.name: Datablock
components.role: mono tag tethered to each blip

components.name: Conflict box
components.role: amber outline that blinks, then holds, around the drifting metric

motion.name: Strip slide-and-clack
motion.how: strips snap into holders with back.out(1.4) in 0.25 s plus a 2 px settle, on the hi-hat at 120 BPM

motion.name: Blip trails
motion.how: linear tracks with three echo dots at 70/45/25% opacity, refreshed every beat

motion.name: Alert pulse
motion.how: conflict outline blinks at 2 Hz for 1 s, then holds solid on the next downbeat

story: Hook: '38 dashboards. One controller.' Strips slap into an overflowing bay, all UNWATCHED. Reveal: the radar fades up, the Acme mark lands as the tower and 'Acme Pulse' types in on the drop. Proof: one blip turns coral inside an amber conflict box; the datablock reads 'Checkout conversion −18% · since 09:42 · after deploy #2231' and its strip slides into HOLD, where the controller taps Roll back. CTA: 'Every metric. Every minute.' over a neat bay of teal strips and a CLEARED stamp, Start free.
adapt: Make each strip one of your objects (a job, an account, a shipment, a pipeline) and let HOLD be whatever your product asks a human to decide.

references.note: colour-coded strips whose position tells the story

fit.risk: Dense at 1:1; cap the bay at 8 strips and the radar at 4–5 blips.
